outcome: complications (blood transfusion, repeat ED visit, failed initial management, hospital admission)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 162 pregnant women presenting to the emergency department with vaginal bleeding and suspected early pregnancy loss, excluding those with gestational age >14 weeks, no evidence of pregnancy loss, uterine cavity anomaly, hemodynamic instability, or hemoglobin <80 g/L.
finding: MUA and EVA showed significantly lower composite complication rates (9% and 10% respectively) compared to expectant management (40%) and misoprostol (33%), with MUA having a significantly shorter mean time to procedure (5.1 hours) than EVA (23.1 hours).
gest_age: Mean gestational age was 66 +- 17 days (approximately 9.4 weeks), with an exclusion criterion of >14 weeks.
